review.title: Recommendation boundary
review.acceptance: The deliverable is a package and information boundary, not a recommender: eligibility is resolved upstream so recommendation can never make content playable, candidate generation may see only the active profile's explicit watchlist, that profile's progress and completion state, catalog metadata and already-resolved eligibility, and it returns content ids plus generator reasons so the reason trail survives the layer most likely to lose it

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 0ac4af8, the reconciled range bbe68ed8..HEAD. (1) npx vitest run --root packages/recommendations -> 4 files, 47 tests, exit 0 (eligibility 10, reasons 11, recommend.property 13, view 13). (2) npx turbo run test --force across the monorepo, cache-busted -> 20/20 tasks, exit 0. (3) npm run typecheck -> 21/21, own invocation, exit 0. ACCEPTANCE CHECKED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE AGAINST THE EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION, AND STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY COUNTING GREEN TESTS -- no gap was found and nothing was implemented this round. CLAUSE 1, eligibility resolved upstream: sealEligibility and resolvedEligibilitySchema mint the EligibleContentId brand; index.ts states that this package cannot mint one and only admits ids upstream already resolved as eligible. CLAUSE 2, recommendation can never make content playable: the package publishes no uri, no provider, no stream descriptor and no availability window anywhere -- grep over the non-test sources finds those words only inside comments explaining their absence -- so there is nothing in its output a player could act on even if a caller wanted it to. CLAUSE 3, candidate generation sees only the four permitted inputs: this is enforced by a TYPE, not by discipline. CandidateGenerator.generate(view: RecommendationView) takes the view and nothing else -- no profile id, no request object, no clock, no repository handle, no second parameter a later change could widen -- and RecommendationView has exactly four members, numbered in its own source: the active profile's eligible watchlist, that profile's progress and completion state, catalog metadata, and the already-resolved eligible id set. CLAUSE 4, output is content ids plus generator reasons: GeneratedCandidate is exactly {contentId: EligibleContentId, reasons: readonly [GeneratorReason, ...GeneratorReason[]]} -- a non-empty reason tuple by type, so the trail cannot be lost at the layer most likely to lose it. A FIFTH PROPERTY WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION, not required by the acceptance but load-bearing for it: no_eligibility_verdict is a separate exclusion code from upstream_not_eligible. Both exclude the work, but the first means the rights pipeline was never asked and the second means it answered no, and reporting the second as the first would tell an operator a work is unlicensed when in fact nobody asked. NO RECOMMENDER WAS BUILT and none is wanted; the acceptance says this is a package and information boundary.

review.title: Optional API-driven autonomous dispatcher
review.acceptance: Optional external agent runner can dispatch queued tasks to configured providers with budgets, audit logs, retries, and human approval gates

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 8166a63, the reconciled range f6c4b942..HEAD. (1) node scripts/cloud/test-dispatcher.mjs -> 35 scenarios, exit 0. (2) npm run test:scripts, which is the alias CI runs and which now includes the dispatcher suite -> 38 env scenarios + 70 control-plane scenarios + 27 workspace-dep groups + 21 turbo-graph groups + 20 validate-repo groups + 35 dispatcher scenarios, exit 0. (3) node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs validate -> valid, 68 tasks, 9 agents. DEFAULT-OFF OBSERVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because an optional spending mechanism that is only documented as off is not evidenced as off: resolveDispatcherConfig over the shipped control/adapters.json returns enabled=false with enableEnvVar=LIBERTY_DISPATCHER_ENABLED, dispatcherIsArmed(cfg, {}) returns false, and dispatcherIsArmed(cfg, {LIBERTY_DISPATCHER_ENABLED: "1"}) ALSO returns false -- the committed switch and the runtime switch must both be on, so arming the environment cannot by itself make a checkout dispatch. ACCEPTANCE CHECKED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE against the existing implementation, and no gap was found, so nothing was implemented this round: configurable providers -> control/adapters.json declares two (openai-responses and agent-bus) with a runner seam in dispatch-runners.mjs; budgets -> budgetDecision, ledgerSpend, estimateCost, the UNREADABLE_LEDGER symbol, perRunCeiling and perTaskCeiling both 0, and a persistent ledger at coordination/agent-bus/dispatch/ledger.json; audit logs -> coordination/agent-bus/dispatch/audit.jsonl, which is also where retry attempts are counted from so the ceiling survives a restart; retries -> retryDecision with maxAttempts 3 and deterministic unjittered backoff; human approval gates -> requiredApprovalCategories and validateApproval, reading escalation.humanOnly from control/policies.json rather than restating it, with an approvals directory the dispatcher cannot write to by construction. Nine refusal codes exist and five of them fire on the shipped configuration at once: dispatcher_disabled, runner_unavailable, cost_unknown, budget_ceiling_not_set and human_approval_missing. NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no live OpenAI runner was added. The openai-responses provider is a declared seam that refuses with runner_unavailable, and cost null refuses independently with cost_unknown. Writing a model-calling runner here would mean shipping a spending path that cannot be exercised or costed from this session, which is the opposite of what the design does on purpose; gpt-architect's round-76 direction says so explicitly.
